questions.question: In a flowchart, which shape holds a Yes/No question that chooses between two paths?
questions.options: an oval | an arrow | a rectangle | a diamond
questions.explanation: The diamond is the decision shape. It asks a Yes/No question, and the answer decides which path the program follows. The oval is only for Start and End.

questions.question: In a quiz game, the score starts at 0 and grows by 10 for every correct answer. What should the programmer use to store the score?
questions.options: a backdrop | a comment | a flowchart | a variable
questions.explanation: A variable is a named box that stores a value that can change — perfect for a score that keeps growing during the game.

questions.question: A program says: IF age > 12 THEN say Teen ELSE say Child. What does it say when age is 10?
questions.options: nothing at all | both words | Teen | Child
questions.explanation: 10 is not greater than 12, so the condition is false. The program takes the ELSE path and says Child.

questions.question: What does iteration mean in programming?
questions.options: writing notes for other programmers | deleting instructions | repeating instructions in a loop | choosing a sprite
questions.explanation: Iteration means repeating. A loop runs the same instructions again and again so you do not have to write them out many times.

questions.question: Which of these values is an integer?
questions.options: two and a half | 3.5 | hello | 25
questions.explanation: An integer is a whole number with no decimal part, like 25. The word hello is a string, and 3.5 has a decimal part so it is not an integer.

questions.question: A programmer writes one named block of instructions for drawing a star, then calls it every time a star is needed. What is this named block called?
questions.options: a procedure | an operator | a condition | a data type
questions.explanation: A procedure (also called a sub-routine) is a named block of instructions you define once and call whenever you need it — no copying and pasting.

questions.question: Amina wants to build a big quiz program, so she first breaks the job into smaller parts: the questions, the scoring and the ending screen. What is this skill called?
questions.options: debugging | iteration | decomposition | initialisation
questions.explanation: Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller parts. Each small part is easier to plan, build and test on its own.

questions.question: Bilal measures how the temperature changes during the day. Which kind of data is temperature?
questions.options: categorical data | a primary key | continuous data | discrete data
questions.explanation: Temperature is measured and can take any value in between, so it is continuous. Counted things like goals are discrete, and favourite colours are categorical.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet formula such as =B2*C2, what does the * symbol mean?
questions.options: add | multiply | divide | delete
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets use the asterisk * for multiply, so =B2*C2 multiplies those two cells together. The / symbol is the one that means divide.

questions.question: A school database stores one complete entry about each pupil: name, class and age. What is each pupil’s complete entry called?
questions.options: a formula | a record | a chart | a field
questions.explanation: One complete entry about one pupil is a record. Each single piece inside it, like the age, is a field.

questions.question: Sara wants to show how a plant’s height changed over six weeks. Which chart shows a change over time best?
questions.options: a pictogram | a pie chart | a tally table | a line graph
questions.explanation: A line graph joins the measurements in order, so you can see the change over time rise and fall at a glance.

questions.question: A scientist needs the temperature of a river recorded every hour, day and night, for a whole month. Which tool should collect the data?
questions.options: a paper form | a data logger | a printer | a pictogram
questions.explanation: A data logger uses a sensor to record measurements automatically, so nobody has to stand by the river all night with a thermometer.

questions.question: In the school network, one central computer stores files and provides services that all the other computers ask for. What is this computer called?
questions.options: a sensor | a packet | a browser | a server
questions.explanation: A server is a computer that provides data and services — such as file storage and programs — to the other devices on a network.

questions.question: When you send a photo across the internet, what happens to the file before it travels?
questions.options: it travels as one giant unbroken block | it is turned into a chart | it is split into small packets that travel separately | it is printed and posted
questions.correctAnswer: it is split into small packets that travel separately
questions.explanation: Files are chopped into small parcels of data called packets. Each packet finds its own way across the network, and they are put back together at the other end.

questions.question: Layla’s message is scrambled before it is sent, so only her friend, who has the key, can read it. What is this scrambling called?
questions.options: spam | bandwidth | streaming | encryption
questions.explanation: Encryption scrambles a message so that only people with the right key can unscramble and read it. It keeps private messages private.

questions.question: Two networks download the same film, and the network with the higher bandwidth finishes first. What does bandwidth measure?
questions.options: how many passwords the network has | how long the network cables are | how much data can travel through the network each second | how bright the screens are
questions.correctAnswer: how much data can travel through the network each second
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the amount of data a network can carry each second. More bandwidth means files and videos arrive faster.

questions.question: An email pretending to be from a bank asks Yusuf to click a link and type in his password. What is this trick called?
questions.options: streaming | encryption | phishing | debugging
questions.explanation: Phishing messages pretend to come from someone you trust to steal private details. Never click the link — close the message and tell a trusted adult.

questions.question: Which of these is software?
questions.options: a drawing app | a mouse | a printer | a hard drive
questions.explanation: Software is the programs and instructions a computer runs, like a drawing app. The mouse, printer and hard drive are hardware — parts you can touch.

questions.question: Deep inside a computer, all data is stored using only two digits. Which two?
questions.options: 2 and 10 | 0 and 1 | 1 and 2 | 0 and 9
questions.explanation: Computers store everything in binary — millions of tiny on/off switches written as the digits 1 and 0.

questions.question: Which of these units of storage is the largest?
questions.options: a byte | a megabyte | a gigabyte | a kilobyte
questions.explanation: From smallest to largest the order is byte, kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte — so the gigabyte is the largest one here.

questions.question: Scratch lets you build programs by snapping coloured blocks together instead of typing code. What kind of programming language is it?
questions.options: a block-based language | a secret language | a spoken language | a text-based language
questions.explanation: In a block-based language like Scratch you drag and snap blocks together. In a text-based language like Python you type every instruction.

questions.question: A factory robot paints cars all day without any human helping it. Which word describes a robot that works by itself?
questions.options: analogue | freeware | autonomous | upgraded
questions.explanation: When a robot carries out its programmed job without help from humans, we say it is autonomous.

questions.question: A script says: REPEAT 4 TIMES, move 10 steps. How far does the sprite move altogether?
questions.options: 10 steps | 14 steps | 4 steps | 40 steps
questions.explanation: A count-controlled loop repeats its instructions a set number of times: 4 repeats of 10 steps is 4 × 10 = 40 steps.

questions.question: In the line IF score > 10 THEN play a fanfare, what does the > symbol check?
questions.options: whether score is a word | whether score is exactly 10 | whether score is greater than 10 | whether score is less than 10
questions.explanation: The > symbol is a comparison operator meaning greater than. The fanfare plays only when the score is bigger than 10.

questions.question: Hodan types B2+B3 into a spreadsheet cell, but nothing is calculated. Which symbol must the formula start with?
questions.explanation: Every spreadsheet formula begins with an equals sign. Typing =B2+B3 tells the software to calculate instead of just showing the letters.

questions.question: A list of raw test scores becomes information when it is…
questions.options: deleted from the computer | organised and given a meaning, like a class average | printed in colour | typed in a bigger font
questions.correctAnswer: organised and given a meaning, like a class average
questions.explanation: Data is raw facts and numbers. When data is organised and explained — like turning scores into a class average — it becomes useful information.

questions.question: At Amina’s house, one box links all the family’s devices to the internet. Which device is it?
questions.options: a printer | a monitor | a router | a data logger
questions.explanation: The router is the device that connects a home or school network to the internet and passes data to the right device.

questions.question: Every website has an IP address made of numbers, yet people type a URL like ehelacademy.com instead. Why?
questions.options: websites have no IP address | letters travel faster than numbers | words are easier for people to remember than long numbers | the numbers are secret
questions.correctAnswer: words are easier for people to remember than long numbers
questions.explanation: Computers find websites by their IP address numbers, but people remember words much more easily — so URLs use words.

questions.question: A greenhouse computer notices when the air gets too hot and opens a window. Which part senses the temperature?
questions.options: a monitor | a keyboard | a sensor | a speaker
questions.explanation: A sensor is an input device that measures changes around it, such as heat, light or movement, and sends the reading to the computer.

questions.question: Which of these is an output device?
questions.options: a mouse | a keyboard | a speaker | a microphone
questions.explanation: Output goes OUT of the computer to you — a speaker gives out sound. The keyboard, mouse and microphone all send input INTO the computer.

questions.question: Hassan writes clear steps, in the right order, telling exactly how to make tea. In computing, what is a list of steps like this called?
questions.options: a password | a database | an algorithm | a website
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a set of step-by-step instructions in the right order. Computers follow algorithms one step at a time.

questions.question: Which of these is an input device — a part you use to put information INTO a computer?
questions.options: a speaker | a keyboard | a printer | a screen
questions.explanation: You type on a keyboard to send letters and numbers into the computer, so it is an input device. Screens, speakers and printers give information out.

questions.question: A website Khalid does not know asks for his full name and home address. What should he do?
questions.options: type it in quickly | keep his personal information private and tell a trusted adult | share a friend’s address instead | post the address in the comments
questions.correctAnswer: keep his personal information private and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Your name and address are personal information. Keep them private online, and tell a trusted adult when a website asks for them.

questions.question: A class database of names is sorted in ascending order. Which of these names comes first?
questions.options: Abdi | Maryam | Zahra | Omar
questions.explanation: Ascending order goes from A to Z. Abdi starts with A, so it comes before Maryam, Omar and Zahra.

questions.question: How does data travel in a Wi-Fi (wireless) network?
questions.options: by radio waves through the air | by light from the screen | on USB sticks carried by hand | through ethernet cables
questions.correctAnswer: by radio waves through the air
questions.explanation: Wireless means no wires — Wi-Fi sends data through the air using radio waves. Wired networks use ethernet cables instead.

questions.question: In a Caesar cipher every letter shifts one place along the alphabet, so A becomes B. What does the word CAT become?
questions.options: DBU | TAC | CBU | DAT
questions.explanation: Shift each letter one place along: C becomes D, A becomes B and T becomes U. So CAT is written as the secret word DBU.
